hints: Use the work-energy principle: the loss in gravitational potential energy during the fall equals the gain in kinetic energy plus the work done against air resistance.
Calculate the loss in gravitational potential energy using $\Delta E_p = mgh$ with $m = 0.6\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $h = 8\text{ m}$.
Calculate the gain in kinetic energy from rest to $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ using $\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$.
Subtract the kinetic energy gain from the potential energy loss to determine the work done against air resistance: $W_{\text{res}} = \Delta E_p - \Delta E_k$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the loss in gravitational potential energy as the particle falls through height $h = 8\text{ m}$:
$$\Delta E_p = mgh = 0.6 \times 10 \times 8 = 48\text{ J}$$

Calculate the gain in kinetic energy from rest ($u = 0$) to final speed $v = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.6 \times 10^2 = 0.3 \times 100 = 30\text{ J}$$

Apply the work-energy principle to find the work done against air resistance:
$$W_{\text{res}} = \Delta E_p - \Delta E_k = 48 - 30 = 18\text{ J}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the work-energy principle for a falling body subject to resistive forces:
$$\text{Loss in Potential Energy} = \text{Gain in Kinetic Energy} + \text{Work Done Against Resistance}$$

Write the formula for gravitational potential energy:
$$E_p = mgh$$

Substitute the mass $m = 0.6\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and height $h = 8\text{ m}$ into the potential energy equation:
$$\Delta E_p = 0.6 \times 10 \times 8 = 6 \times 8 = 48\text{ J}$$

Write the formula for kinetic energy:
$$E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$$

Substitute the mass $m = 0.6\text{ kg}$ and final speed $v = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$\Delta E_k = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.6 \times (10)^2 = 0.3 \times 100 = 30\text{ J}$$

Rearrange the work-energy relation to make work done against resistance the subject by subtracting $\Delta E_k$ from both sides:
$$W_{\text{res}} = \Delta E_p - \Delta E_k$$

Substitute the calculated energy values:
$$W_{\text{res}} = 48 - 30 = 18\text{ J}$$
